name: Fool (Milton Bradley)
description: Fool is a classic card game published by Milton Bradley (MB Games) that combines shedding mechanics with bluffing and social deduction. Similar to 'Cheat' or 'I Doubt It', the objective is to discard all your cards by playing them face-down and declaring their rank. However, if another player suspects you are lying, they can shout 'Fool!'. It is a fast-paced game of deception, memory, and psychological warfare.

history.origins: Derived from the much older international game 'Cheat' (also known as Bullshit). Milton Bradley branded it as 'Fool' to make it a family-friendly parlor game.
timeline: 1970s: MB Games releases 'Fool' as part of their 'Classic Series'.
1980s: Variations with special 'fool' cards or tokens are introduced.
Present: Remains a popular choice for families who want a less 'obscene' version of the bluffing classic.
20th Century: The game was widely exported and translated into several languages with the same 'Fool' branding.
history.cultural: Represents the 'party game' era of Milton Bradley's dominance in the tabletop market.
history.evolution: The game moved from a loose folk game to a structured commercial product with specific rules about 'illegal joy' or 'talking out of turn' in some versions.

setup.dealing: The entire deck is dealt out to all players as evenly as possible.

rules.objective: Be the first player to get rid of all your cards by playing them face-down to the center pile and declaring their rank in sequence (Aces through Kings); you may bluff, but if challenged and caught you take the pile.
rules.gameplay:
1. The first player plays any number of cards face-down and declares they are 'Aces'.
2. The next player must play/declare '2s', then '3s', and so on up to 'Kings', then back to 'Aces'.
3. You can play cards that ARE NOT the declared rank, but you must LIE and say they are.
keyRules: Entire deck dealt evenly to all players. Play face-down and declare rank in sequence (Aces, 2s, up to Kings, then Aces). You may bluff. Any player may call 'Fool!' to challenge; if wrong they take the pile, if right the declarer takes the pile. First to empty hand wins.

strategy.basic: Tell the truth when the pile is small. There is little reward and high risk to lying when only 4 cards are in the center. Save your big bluffs for when you have a 10-card hand of junk and the pile is massive.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Pile-Seeding' Maneuver: If you have four Jacks, and the current rank is Jacks, play all four of them truthful. This 'cleans' the pile for you and ensures the next player MUST lie (as you have all the Jacks). If you call 'Fool!' on them immediately, they take the pile you just emptied.
strategy.advanced: Body-Language Reading: Most players have a 'tell' when playing multiple cards. Watch for the timing of their hand movement. If they play three cards as 'Aces' very slowly, they are likely searching for a lie.
tips: Keep track of the cards you've seen. If you have been forced to pick up the pile, YOU are the most powerful person at the table because you know what's in your hand.
If you are down to one card, everyone will call 'Fool!' on you regardless. Try to hold a card of the expected rank for your final turn.
